newsitem.title: CHINA: China to take measure to boost real estate market.
newsitem.headline: China to take measure to boost real estate market.

text.p: China will take measures, including cuts in real estate trading tax, to boost its bearish nationwide real estate market by the end of 1996, the Business News said on Thursday.

The measures include cutting the real estate trading tax, increasing loans to developers, easing restrictions on loans for buyers and encouraging developers to cut prices of their vacant commercial apartments, the newspaper said but gave no further details.

By the end of 1995, China had about 35 million square metres of vacant apartments in its cities, worth 82 billion yuan, up from 23.54 million square metres a year earlier, the Economic Daily has reported.
The government wants developers to build more homes within the price range of the average citizen. Most of the vacant homes are affordable only to a small class of rich people.
